objects.say: The bolt comes back, and the grille that the boys have looked through for years swings open.^It was never locked against thieves. It was locked against boys, which takes a better bolt.
The bolt comes back, and the grille that the boys have looked through for years swings open.^It was never locked against thieves. It was locked against boys, which takes a better bolt.

objects.text: The watch's book: who stood which night.^Forty nights back it stops. The last line says: {t}AZAR. GATE. (CHECK ON HIM.){/}| Nobody did.
The lookout's stool, under the window.^From here a man can see the whole of Ashkel, and nothing in it moving.| It is the dullest watch anybody ever stood, and you have stood most of them.

objects.say: The key turns. The cell door swings.^It is the first time in the history of the watch that anybody has broken INTO the lock-up.
The cell keys, on a peg within reach of the cell.^The watch has never lost a prisoner this way. The watch has never had a prisoner who was awake.

objects.text: Cedar, in the log, stacked to the beams.^The Temple paid for it twice. Ilu-Bani delivered it once. Both sides call this the usual arrangement.

objects.say: A bar of cedar as thick as an arm, in bronze hooks. It lifts out.^Ilu-Bani barred his door against the whole of Ashkel. He did not think to bar his cellar against the watch house.

objects.text: A boy's lines. {t}I WILL NOT SLEEP IN CLASS.{/} Thirty-one times, neat as you like.^The thirty-second trails off down the tablet and over the edge.
A jar with a cloth tied over it, and holes in the cloth.^Inside, a frog, asleep. It was confiscated forty-one nights ago. It has had the best of it.

objects.say: A bronze bolt, on this side only, well oiled.^The master comes in by the roof, with a jug, when the boys have gone home. This is how he leaves.

objects.text: A man's sandals, by the door, toes to the street.^They have been oiled every week for forty years. They have not been anywhere.
Figs in honey. Figs in wine. Figs dried on a string.^She has not eaten a fig in forty years. She says she is keeping them.
In here the sandals are wet, and there is dust on them from the road.^It is the only room in Ashkel that is tidier asleep than awake, and it is the one she never goes into.

Lamp oil, to the brim, in jars taller than a boy.^He keeps it in the dark, on purpose. You are standing in it holding the Wakefire.| You stand very still, and then you leave the way you would leave a sleeping bull.
